Lockdown Blue Light Brigade

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We investigate a brazen blue light gang operating in JHb, and ask why neither the police nor the national lockdown has stopped them in their tracks

Unique Selling Point:
A brazen gang of car hijackers are operating along the R59 hi-way just south of Johannesburg, pretending to be police and pulling over unwitting motorists in supposed traffic stops, before kidnapping them, holding them hostage while their bank accounts are drained and then making off with their valuables and their vehicles. And while its been an ongoing issue, the most recent cases have all taken place under the national lockdown.

Summary:
For the past few years a notorious Blue Light Gang have been terrorising the streets of Johannesburg - and by their unique modus operandi police believe it most likely is the same group of people behind dozens of attacks. Their plan is simple - after identifying vehicles they want to hijack, in most cases expensive double cab bakkies, they follow the victims on the highway in an unmarked white vehicle equipped with blue flashing lights on the dashboard. Motorists think they are being pulled over by legitimate police / traffic police. Once stopped a single man, dressed in police uniform approaches the vehicle. Initially motorists are questioned as if its a real traffic stop - asked for their drivers licence, told they were speeding, asked if they have been drinking etc etc. Then the driver is ordered out of the vehicle, and once that happens several more armed men appear, seemingly out of nowhere, and take the hapless motorist and anyone else in the car hostage at gunpoint. They are driven to an abandoned piece of veldt, held hostage and forced to hand over their bank card details. Their vehicles are also searched for tracking devices. Some victims are assaulted, and almost all of them are held for at least four to six hours. Once the hijackers are ready to leave, the victims are told in which direction to walk to find help. the blue light gang make off with their vehicles, phones, wallets, wedding rings etc.

Further information:
Many of our case studies are extremely upset about the treatment they receive at police stations in the areas of the hijackings after the traumatic experiences.

We know of at least 8 cases in the last 12 months, but according to a SAPS insider their are many many more over several years

Because the hijackings take place along the hiway at different places, the cases go to different police stations and SAPS took a very long time to connect the dots

A task team has been assigned the case as of May 2020 - they might be willing to do an interview and discuss the difficulties they face in catching the gang

Script:


Lockdown Blue Light Gang
10 August 2020
First Draft Script

Voice
According to the latest crime statistics, vehicle hijackings in South Africa are up a worrying 13.3% compared to last year. And while most of us are all too aware of the constant danger, what do you do when the hijackers come disguised as the very people we rely on to save us from these types of crimes?

Link Mac
South Africans are no strangers to so-called “Blue Light Gangs” - where armed criminals dressed as policeman hijack unsuspecting motorists. But here in the south of Johannesburg an alarming new trend is emerging - this is where members of the public are not only being hijacked, but also kidnapped and held hostage for hours on end.

Voice
One of the current hotspots is the R59 hi-way - a major route for thousands of daily commuters travelling between Johannesburg and towns like Vereeniging, Van der Bijl Park and Sasolburg in the Vaal Triangle. And the National Lockdown has done little to curb the criminals. George and Belinda Visser from Sasolburg came face to face with a blue light gang on the R59 in May.

Sound Up George Visser
So we left Johannesburg at around about six o clock in the evening, travelling back to the Vaal.

Voice
The couple had helped their son move house to Johannesburg earlier that day. Visser says they were in a hurry to get home before the 8pm lockdown curfew.

Sound Up George
George: And so we were travelling quite fast, and then we exited Alberton going to towards Vereeniging. And all of a sudden there were blue lights behind us, and I knew I was travelling fast, and it is lockdown. So I pulled over.

Voice
Visser had no reason to suspect the man who approached his double cab toyota was anything other than a real policeman - even the white Volkswagen Golf car with the flashing blue lights looked legit.

Sound Up George
When I looked into the rearview mirror you could see there were markings on the vehicle, definitely, police markings. But he started asking me for my drivers license, so he’s asking me some questions, putting me at ease.

Voice
Convinced it was a routine traffic stop, Visser thought nothing of the man asking him whether they had a firearm in the vehicle.

Sound Up George
And my wife, she carries a firearm with her, so I said yes.

Voice
The “supposed” policeman said he wanted to match the serial number on the firearm to the serial number on the gun license.

Sound Up George
So I actually took out this firearm, I made it safe for him, I passed it over to him, and in this time a second person appears on my wife’s side.

Voice
What followed was one of the most traumatic experiences of their lives.

Sound Up George
And within seconds there’s four guys. Well actually one jumped onto my wife with a firearm, and two jumped into the back and they are now starting to strangle me, and putting something over my head, so you can’t see, you can’t breath because they’re strangling you.

Voice
Visser was loaded into the back seat of the vehicle, and with the hapless couple held at gunpoint, the hijackers drove them to a secluded veldt a few kilometers away. Once there, they were forced to handover their valuables, before being tied up and threatened with their lives.

Sound Up George
George: When we got to a standstill we got thrown out, tied up, but now one guy stays with us with a firearm all the time. And my wife is talking to me and obviously she’s in panic, saying they’re going to shoot us, they are going to kill us, and I said to her please just keep calm. Because this guy, when he hears you talking, he’s shouting…

Mac: He get’s aggressive…

George: … and he’s pointing a gun and he’s aggressive now.

Voice
While the gunman held them hostage, other members of the gang were tearing up the inside of the bakkie in search of the tracking device.

Sound Up George
The other guys are now obviously looking for the tracker, and then they bring our wallets. And so they obviously take out all our bank cards, and now they are asking for pin numbers.

Voice
The couple were warned to give the correct pin numbers or face dire consequences.

Sound Up George
So we gave them our pins because they tell you we’re going to send one guy now to the bank. And if he doesn’t get money, they are going to shoot you.

Voice
The Vissers were hijacked at about 6:30pm, but by 11:30 that evening - some 5 hours into the ordeal - they were still being held at gunpoint in the freezing cold veldt.

Sound Up George
So they wanted to waste some time to get to twelve o clock that evening. So that your daily limit expires, and they can draw some money again. That was the whole idea.

Voice
The hijackers got away with R60 000 in cash, the brand new bakkie, and all the valuables the Vissers had on them. Thankfully they were eventually set free, and made their way on foot to the Kliprivier police station a few hours later.



Link Macfarlane
Not stopping if you are ever pulled over by real police could have dire consequences, so is there anything motorists can do to prevent themselves from falling victim to these types of crimes?

Voice
Richard Brussouw spent nearly 30 years in the South African police service before starting the National Hijacking Prevention Academy in 2001. He says that when it comes to preventing blue light hijackings, step one is to realise that the gangs are looking for motorists who are committing minor traffic infringements while driving.

Sound Up Richard Brussouw
The robber wants your brain to say oh sh… and the way they do that is they target the cars where they commit the most common traffic offences. That could be speeding, doing a lane change without indicating, and most common - on your cellphone. I come behind you, I put the blue light on, your brain goes defensive mode, oh sh…, you’re going to stop.

Link Macfarlane
And the criminals are growing ever more brazen - according to our sources there were four incidents in a single week on the R59 at the beginning of this month.

Voice
Specialist private security contractor Carl Dentry from Sebenzani Security, who regularly assist the police in bringing hijackers on the streets of Johannesburg to book, says blue light incidents along this hi-way are an all too common occurrence.

Sound Up Carl Dentry
Mac: When you say it’s been ongoing for quite some time, how long have you been following it for?

Carl: I’d say the last five, six months.

Voice
Since the gang seem to be operating with absolute impunity, we asked Sebenzani to accompany us to this desolate stretch of veldt along the R59, where Colin Sampson from Johannesburg also fell victim to the blue light gang in September last year. Getting to the sight in broad daylight is already a daunting experience, but Sampson says doing so in pitch darkness while being held at gunpoint is absolutely terrifying.

Sound Up Colin
Mac: Can’t imagine what it must be like in the dead of the night to be somewhere here?

Colin: Ja, it’s dark…

Voice
It was Sampson’s first time back at the scene since his ordeal, and he found this set of baseball gloves that were in his white Toyota Fortuner the night he was hijacked. The veldt is obviously used regularly, because we also found various car parts and and these cable ties lying around - an ominous reminder of the gang’s M.O.

Sound Up Colin
It was a friday night, I was coming from the airport, I landed at about eight, so I got here, round about this area, at about nine o clock.

Voice
Although months apart, both Sampson and George Visser’s incidents took place within a few kilometers of the Kliprivier offramp on the R59.

Sound Up Colin
Blue lights came up behind me, I automatically pulled over to the side, a person dressed in a police uniform got out, came to the side of the window, I opened the window just a little bit, he said we just want to make sure everything is ok and then I want to let you get back on your way.

Voice
Sampson says he was aware of blue light incidents in the area at the time.

Sound Up Colin
I told him that I was worried because there were a lot of stories about this type of hijacking, he said no he understands, that’s exactly why they are doing this, he just wanted to check that everything was ok and then he would let me get on my.

Voice
The man in police uniform told Sampson to get out of the vehicle and show him what was in the boot of the car.

Sound Up Colin
And as I opened the boot, the guy dressed in police uniform said to me is that your laptop, and I knew there was something wrong, and I said no, no, no wait, and there was about five guys, they took me around to the passenger side of the car, shoved me into the back of the car.

Voice
The other gang members had emerged from the blue light car, this time a white Audi sedan. The men sped off with Sampson held at gunpoint on the back seat of his vehicle. Then, incredibly, the vehicle was brought to a stop a short while later and two other men, also hijacking victims from a separate vehicle, were thrown onto the rear seat with Sampson.

Sound Up Colin
Colin: They were busy hijacking another car.

Mac: Hold on, so after they hijacked you they went and did another hijacking?

Colin: Ja, so I don’t think it was the same Audi that hijacked me, but it was obviously the same crew. They hijacked two black guys in a white double cab, one guy tried to run away, they obviously hit him with a gun, and then put him into my car as well. So there were three of us hijacked victims in the car. Then they basically travelled north on the R59 and then we went off the hiway, and we came to basically this spot, in the dark, travelling slowly, so that nobody would recognise them, it was pitch, pitch black.

Voice
While the victims were cable-tied and held at gunpoint in the veldt, the two hijacked vehicles were searched for valuables and their tracking systems.

Sound Up Colin
And they proceeded to take everything out of our cars, the panels off the door, they took the polystyrene and anything in the vehicle off, to find the trackers.

Voice
It took the hijackers hours to disable the tracking systems, before they finally made off with the stolen vehicles. The three victims were left traumatised but relatively unharmed in the veldt. Eventually the men were also able to make their way to the nearby Kliprivier police station to report the incident. Provincial spokesperson Brigadier Mathapelo Peters says the police have now established a special task force to combat blue light gangs operating in Gauteng.



Sound Up Brig Mathapelo Peters
Brigadier: The South African Police Service in Gauteng is aware of these blue light hijackings, we actually have a task team that has been assigned to work on these cases.

Mac: Can you perhaps give us any official stats as to how many cases have been reported there?

Brigadier: At this stage I cannot give stats, I am not authorised to do that. But I can confirm that at provincial level we are sitting with 48 cases that are being investigated, and 25 of these are already in court. And we have arrested 27 suspects on these cases. But I must indicate that this is not only on the R59, its all cases that have been reported across Gauteng.

Voice
But until hijackings like these are completely eradicated from our streets, Brussouw has some final tips.

Sound Up Brussouw
If you’re in motion, try and communicate with somebody, phone the emergency numbers 10111, Vodacom 112. If you’ve got a tracking device in your vehicle, and its got an assist button that you can press, press it. You want to communicate now and tell somebody what is currently happening at that point.

Voice
And if you do find yourself in the unfortunate position of facing armed hijackers, remember that your car is not worth your life.

Sound Up Brussouw
You must keep in mind, there are two, three men around your motor car now. Adrenalin is pumping, they are not breathing properly. It takes a split second for that robber to misread something and accidentally a trigger is pulled. Most shootings occur when people resist, or there is a wrong movement, hand movement, where the robber misreads this. So try and stay calm, not too fast hand movements, and show the robber that you are no threat to him.




Promo 1
Voice
Hijacked, held hostage and extorted at gunpoint - the terrifying experiences of motorists in Johannesburg who’ve fallen victim to a blue light gang’s reign of terror despite the national lockdown.

Promo 2
Voice
Imagine rushing home to beat the lockdown curfew when suddenly you are pulled over by a police vehicle, only to discover that you’ve become the latest victim of a dangerous blue light gang in Johannesburg.

Promo 3
Voice
On the hi-way south of Johannesburg, motorists are being hijacked, kidnapped and held hostage by a ruthless gang of criminals. Blue light gangs are back, and more terrifying than ever.

Then they basically travelled north on the R59 and then we went off the hiway, and we came to basically this spot, in the dark, travelling slowly, so that nobody would recognise them, it was pitch, pitch black. Voice While the victims were cable-tied and held at gunpoint in the veldt, the two hijacked vehicles were searched for valuables and their tracking systems. Sound Up Colin And they proceeded to take everything out of our cars, the panels off the door, they took the polystyrene and anything in the vehicle off, to find the trackers. Voice It took the hijackers hours to disable the tracking systems, before they finally made off with the stolen vehicles. The three victims were left traumatised but relatively unharmed in the veldt. Eventually the men were also able to make their way to the nearby Kliprivier police station to report the incident. Provincial spokesperson Brigadier Mathapelo Peters says the police have now established a special task force to combat blue light gangs operating in Gauteng. Sound Up Brig Mathapelo Peters Brigadier: The South African Police Service in Gauteng is aware of these blue light hijackings, we actually have a task team that has been assigned to work on these cases. Mac: Can you perhaps give us any official stats as to how many cases have been reported there? Brigadier: At this stage I cannot give stats, I am not authorised to do that. But I can confirm that at provincial level we are sitting with 48 cases that are being investigated, and 25 of these are already in court. And we have arrested 27 suspects on these cases. But I must indicate that this is not only on the R59, its all cases that have been reported across Gauteng. Voice But until hijackings like these are completely eradicated from our streets, Brussouw has some final tips. Sound Up Brussouw If you’re in motion, try and communicate with somebody, phone the emergency numbers 10111, Vodacom 112. If you’ve got a tracking device in your vehicle, and its got an assist button that you can press, press it. You want to communicate now and tell somebody what is currently happening at that point. Voice And if you do find yourself in the unfortunate position of facing armed hijackers, remember that your car is not worth your life. Sound Up Brussouw You must keep in mind, there are two, three men around your motor car now. Adrenalin is pumping, they are not breathing properly. It takes a split second for that robber to misread something and accidentally a trigger is pulled. Most shootings occur when people resist, or there is a wrong movement, hand movement, where the robber misreads this. So try and stay calm, not too fast hand movements, and show the robber that you are no threat to him. Promo 2 Voice Imagine rushing home to beat the lockdown curfew when suddenly you are pulled over by a police vehicle, only to discover that you’ve become the latest victim of a dangerous blue light gang in Johannesburg. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We investigate a brazen blue light gang operating in JHb, and ask why neither the police nor the national lockdown has stopped them in their tracks
metadata.Unique Selling Point: A brazen gang of car hijackers are operating along the R59 hi-way just south of Johannesburg, pretending to be police and pulling over unwitting motorists in supposed traffic stops, before kidnapping them, holding them hostage while their bank accounts are drained and then making off with their valuables and their vehicles. And while its been an ongoing issue, the most recent cases have all taken place under the national lockdown.
metadata.Summary: For the past few years a notorious Blue Light Gang have been terrorising the streets of Johannesburg - and by their unique modus operandi police believe it most likely is the same group of people behind dozens of attacks. Their plan is simple - after identifying vehicles they want to hijack, in most cases expensive double cab bakkies, they follow the victims on the highway in an unmarked white vehicle equipped with blue flashing lights on the dashboard. Motorists think they are being pulled over by legitimate police / traffic police. Once stopped a single man, dressed in police uniform approaches the vehicle. Initially motorists are questioned as if its a real traffic stop - asked for their drivers licence, told they were speeding, asked if they have been drinking etc etc. Then the driver is ordered out of the vehicle, and once that happens several more armed men appear, seemingly out of nowhere, and take the hapless motorist and anyone else in the car hostage at gunpoint. They are driven to an abandoned piece of veldt, held hostage and forced to hand over their bank card details. Their vehicles are also searched for tracking devices. Some victims are assaulted, and almost all of them are held for at least four to six hours. Once the hijackers are ready to leave, the victims are told in which direction to walk to find help. the blue light gang make off with their vehicles, phones, wallets, wedding rings etc.
metadata.Further information: Many of our case studies are extremely upset about the treatment they receive at police stations in the areas of the hijackings after the traumatic experiences. We know of at least 8 cases in the last 12 months, but according to a SAPS insider their are many many more over several years Because the hijackings take place along the hiway at different places, the cases go to different police stations and SAPS took a very long time to connect the dots A task team has been assigned the case as of May 2020 - they might be willing to do an interview and discuss the difficulties they face in catching the gang
